corrections: ⛔ THE BIGGEST ONE — FIX (a) DOES NOT CLOSE THE VECTOR, AND THE REPORT'S OWN QUOTED EVIDENCE REFUTES ITS RATIONALE. It says forcing cause:'player' means "the cheat becomes the honest, priced action". There is no honest priced action any more: the comment the report itself quotes at controls.ts:1201-1204 ends "A player can no longer buy a guaranteed cut, and against a component of 7+ connectors a raid cannot sever at all." Under fix (a) a modified client can still buy guaranteed cuts nobody else in the game can buy — `player.ts:342-345` still accrues `disruptionCharges` (`BUILD_ACTIONS_PER_CHARGE = 5`, constants.ts:304) up to `MAX_DISRUPTION_CHARGES = 2` (constants.ts:305), and `computeBaseCharge` (disruptionManager.ts:135-145) charges exactly 1 per hostile cut (2 for a defensive combo, constants.ts:312) with NO enemy check and NO accumulated damage. Worse, `if (!isHostile) return 0;` (disruptionManager.ts:139) makes severs of the cheater's OWN colour free and unbounded. Fix (a) collapses the rate from 90-per-burst to ~2-per-recharge-cycle; it does not reach zero. Say that in the brief, or the owner will approve a fix believing it is a closure.

⛔ `four_sites_risk` IS FACTUALLY WRONG ABOUT `cause`, even though its conclusion for THIS fix survives. It states "there is no factory, no serialize, no hash contribution and no worker projection for it." `cause` is serialized: the SerializedEffect type declares it at save.ts:577, `serializeEffect` emits `cause: e.cause,` at save.ts:2328, `deserializeEffect` restores `cause: s.cause,` at save.ts:2408 — and save.ts:584 is a docblock naming them as "These four sites". world.ts:227-231 says it outright: "⚠ THIS IS A THIRD UNION … the ACTION cause and the EFFECT cause (`effects.ts`, `save.ts`) are separate declarations that must agree." SPARK_CANON.md §6 records the S182 46→47 bump as being FOR a new `cause` value. The correct statement is narrow: this fix adds no new cause value and touches no wire field, so PROTOCOL_VERSION stays 47 — not that `cause` has no serialize sites. Left as written, the next session that adds a cause value reads this and skips two of four sites.

⚠ THERE IS NO "HOSTILE-AUTH GATE". The fix rationale says forcing 'player' "routes straight into the existing hostile-auth + disruption-charge gate at disruptionManager.ts:103-112". Lines 103-112 are only `const player = world.players.get(action.playerId); if (player === undefined) return false;` and the charge comparison at :111. `isHostile` (disruptionManager.ts:138) selects the PRICE, it is not an authorization. There is no ownership or enemy gate on the sever path at all — which is the report's own finding #6, contradicted by its own fix_shape three paragraphs later.

net_assessment:
The report's core is SOUND and I could not refute its central claim: at 7d1514b, `SEVER_BOND` is wire-reachable (protocol.ts:1545), payload-unvalidated (protocol.ts:1712-1719), re-derives only `playerId` (intentStamp.ts:23), and seven of eight `cause` values bypass every gate unconditionally (disruptionManager.ts:81-101) with no ownership check in the reducer (severBond.ts:53-63), bounded only by a 90-token bucket (constants.ts:935). All 18 findings verified against the tree; 17 CONFIRMED, 1 PARTIAL (the fix-(c) red-test list is incomplete, not wrong). It also correctly self-limits with two severity collapses that both check out, and correctly refuses fix (b) on evidence the code itself records. That is materially better work than this project's S161 sweep.

Three things must be corrected before this goes to the owner, in order of consequence. FIRST, the recommended fix is presented as a closure and it is not: forcing `cause:'player'` leaves a modified client able to buy up to 2 guaranteed enemy cuts per recharge (charges still accrue, player.ts:342-345; no enemy check, disruptionManager.ts:135-145) and unlimited free self-severs — a capability owner ruling R78 deliberately removed from honest players, as the very comment the report quotes says. It is a ~45× rate collapse, not a fix, and the owner's yes/no should be asked on that basis. SECOND, `four_sites_risk` asserts `cause` has no serialize site; it has three (save.ts:577/2328/2408) plus a docblock naming them, and world.ts:227 calls it "A THIRD UNION" — the conclusion survives only because this fix adds no new value, and the wrong sentence is exactly the kind that rots into the next session's four-sites failure. THIRD, the enumeration the project prizes most is off in two places: `bombLifecycle.ts:146` is an ARCHIVED subsystem (canon §1) and `severActor`'s own docblock names two 'player'-cause dispatchers (controls.ts, botController.ts) that no longer exist — which, corrected, makes the "no honest player notices" argument stronger, not weaker.

Missed hazards worth adding to the brief: the tolerant-default consumer at severToastRenderer.ts:176 (the exact S182 lesson-7 shape it was told to hunt for), the second existing test of the helper at hostmigD4.test.ts:125-137, the absence of ANY test on the host INTENT pipeline (no `hostHandlers.test.ts` exists — so the proposed fix will be pinned only at the helper unless someone builds that fixture), and the four-site cost of the "cheap" diagnostics counter, alongside a pre-existing leak it exposed (`actorEliminated` is reset nowhere while `actorBenched` is reset twice, gameMode.ts:167/425). Size: Micro is defensible for the edit and at its ceiling for the tests as written.
